papers.title: Error Analysis of Krylov Subspace approximation Based on IDR($s$) Method for Matrix Function Bilinear Forms
authors: Qianqian Xue, Xiaoqiang Yue, Xian-Ming Gu
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2509.08563v4 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The matrix function bilinear form, namely $\mathbf{u}^\top f(A)\mathbf{v}$, appears in many scientific computing problems, where $\mathbf{u}, \mathbf{v} \in \mathbb{R}^n$, $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$, and $f(z)$ is a given analytic function. The Induced Dimension Reduction (IDR($s$)) method was originally proposed to solve a large system of linear equations, and effectively reduces the complexity and storage requirement by dimensionality reduction while maintaining the numerical stability of the algorithm. In fact, the IDR($s$) method can generate an interesting Hessenberg decomposition. papers.title: Entry growth in Gaussian elimination
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2608.19189v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Gaussian elimination is one of the oldest algorithms in mathematics, and the most popular method for solving an unstructured linear system. Its stability in finite precision is controlled by its growth factor, which measures how large the entries produced during elimination can become. Understanding the worst-case behavior of this quantity has been a central problem in numerical analysis since the 1940s.
  Here we make a significant leap in that understanding, settling several open problems. In particular, we determine the asymptotic behavior of the maximum growth factor under complete and rook pivoting, proving that both are quasi-polynomial in dimension.
